  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Teams, fan-outs and background sessions}

---



Use a team for several roles working on one task, a fan-out for the same task over several
inputs, or `gptr_parallel()` for independently specified calls. Each returns a session whose
children can be inspected. The reactor overlaps model I/O; ordinary inline R code still
executes in the one R process.

The following examples use scripted providers with the inline backend, without network calls
or worker/CLI processes. Real-model, background and rewind recipes are not executed.

## A team of named roles


``` r
library(gptr)
reviewer = gptr_fake_provider(list("A scripted review; check the actual analysis separately."),
                              name = "reviewer")
reviews = peter("Review the analysis workflow.", model = reviewer, envir = new.env(),
                 agents = list(
                   statistics = gptr_agent(system = "Check the statistical assumptions.",
                                           backend = "inline"),
                   code = gptr_agent(system = "Check the code and input/output handling.",
                                     backend = "inline")
                 ))
reviews$kind
#> [1] "team"
names(reviews$children)
#> [1] "statistics" "code"
reviews$statistics$text
#> [1] "A scripted review; check the actual analysis separately."
reviews$code$status
#> [1] "idle"
```

The member names identify roles. `gptr_agent()` can specify each role's model, system text,
tools, skills, backend and exported object names. A multi-member inline team uses child
workspace overlays: ordinary assignments stay in each child until requested exports are
collected. That is not a security boundary or protection against arbitrary code mutating an
external resource. Worker backends use separate R processes and serialize selected inputs;
CLI backends need their external CLI and authentication.

`reviews$text` joins member reports under headings; `reviews$value` is their named list of
values, and `reviews$statistics` is the member session. A report is model-generated output,
not verification. Inspect each child's status and the actual results before relying on it.

Continuing a team without `agents =` asks the container's model to synthesize those reports:


``` r
reviews |> peter("Reconcile the reviews into one prioritized list of fixes.")
```

This adds a model request. `agents =` starts new children; it cannot be used to continue a
piped session. Teams and fan-outs run in the foreground and cannot be combined with
`background = TRUE`, `.run = FALSE`, or nested as `gptr_parallel()` members.

## A fan-out over input elements


``` r
cohorts = list(A = 1:3, B = 4:6, C = 7:9)
cohort_model = gptr_fake_provider(list("A scripted cohort summary."), name = "cohort")
summaries = peter("Summarize this cohort.", cohorts, model = cohort_model,
                  envir = new.env(), parallel = 2, .opts = list(backend = "inline"))
summaries$kind
#> [1] "fanout"
summaries$text
#>                            A                            B
#> "A scripted cohort summary." "A scripted cohort summary."
#>                            C
#> "A scripted cohort summary."
vapply(summaries$children, function(child) child$status, "")
#>      A      B      C
#> "idle" "idle" "idle"
```

`parallel = 2` limits active children, not the number of inputs processed: every element is
queued. Exactly one attached context object must supply the batch, as a list, atomic vector
or data-frame rows. Each child receives its own element. Unique nonempty element names become
child names; otherwise positions are used. Inspect a child with `summaries$A` or
`summaries[[1]]`.

For object-producing work, keep each child's results separate and specify exports only when
needed. Export-name collisions are reported and results are collected in task order; this
is not an automatic merge of competing analyses.

## Independent calls with gptr_parallel()


``` r
team = gptr_parallel(
  planner = peter("Plan the analysis.",
               model = gptr_fake_provider(list("A scripted plan."), name = "planner"),
               envir = new.env()),
  review = peter("Review the inputs.",
                 model = gptr_fake_provider(list("A scripted input review."), name = "inputs"),
                 envir = new.env()),
  max_active = 2
)
team$planner$text
#> [1] "A scripted plan."
team$review$text
#> [1] "A scripted input review."
```

The calls are deferred while the members are constructed, then scheduled together. You can
also pass `.list =` a named list of sessions created with `.run = FALSE`. Member names must
not collide with session accessors such as `text` or `status`. A member must be idle with
queued input, rather than an already completed call passed by variable.

Each member retains its own model and workspace, but member `tools =`, `budget =` and
per-run `.opts` (including `max_turns`) are not applied. The team shares the governing root
budget. Set applicable defaults before launch or run under an enclosing budget; see the
token-efficiency vignette. `on_error = "return"` keeps failed members for inspection;
`"stop"` signals the first failed member's condition after all members settle.

## Deferred sessions and SDK control

`.run = FALSE` constructs an idle session with queued input without requesting a model yet.
`gptr_step()` advances it by model turns; `gptr_wait()` starts queued work and pumps until
settlement or timeout. Returned sessions can be inspected at each stage.


``` r
staged_model = gptr_fake_provider(list("First answer.", "Answer after the follow-up."),
                                  name = "staged")
staged = peter("Prepare a plan.", model = staged_model, envir = new.env(), .run = FALSE)
staged$status
#> [1] "idle"
staged$turns
#> [1] 0
gptr_step(staged, turns = 1)
staged$text
#> [1] "First answer."

gptr_steer(staged, "Include an input validation step.", as = "follow_up")
gptr_wait(staged, timeout = 10)
staged$text
#> [1] "Answer after the follow-up."
```

A steer reaches a running agent after its current tool results; a follow-up is delivered when
it would otherwise stop. On an idle session, either remains queued until the next run.
Piping a prompt into a running session uses the same steering mechanism. `gptr_wait()` timing
out leaves the run running; it does not cancel it. `gptr_cancel()` aborts active runs, keeps
partial history and leaves idle sessions alone.

`gptr_on(s, event, function(event, ctx) ...)` subscribes to cataloged session events and
returns a function that removes the listener. Keep reporting state outside the agent's
workspace and remove listeners when finished:


``` r
observed = new.env()
observed$roles = character()
tracked = peter("Say hello.", model = gptr_fake_provider(list("Hello."), name = "tracked"),
                envir = new.env(), .run = FALSE)
off = gptr_on(tracked, "message_end", function(event, ctx) {
  observed$roles = c(observed$roles, event$message$role)
  NULL
})
gptr_step(tracked)
off()
observed$roles
#> [1] "user"      "assistant"
```

## Experimental background work

A background session runs through idle-console callbacks from the optional `later` package.
It is not an independent R execution thread. Given an existing fitted model `fit`, start with
a short task and an explicit workspace:


``` r
work = new.env()
work$fit = fit
s = peter("Inspect the model fit and propose follow-up checks.", fit = work$fit, envir = work,
          background = TRUE)
s$status
gptr_jobs()
s |> peter("Prioritize residual diagnostics.")
gptr_wait(s, timeout = 30)
# If it is still running and you want to stop it:
gptr_cancel(s)
```

With `gptr.background_tools = "idle"` (default), an R tool can run at an idle tick and occupy
the R console until it finishes. `"wait"` defers those tools to a blocking gptr call. Rscript,
knitr and Quarto have no idle-console progress: use `gptr_wait()` or another blocking call.
Other front ends have the support limits documented in `help("gptr-background", package = "gptr")`;
do not infer
support from the mere return of a session object.

An approval or question at an idle tick parks the session as `waiting`, without performing
the action. A later blocking call resumes it and the model repeats its request before the
usual prompt. That extra request can use tokens. A waiting session has no active run for
`gptr_cancel()` to abort; inspect its status before choosing how to resume or stop jobs.

## Checkpoints, usage and durable history

After a modifying run, inspect checkpoints and preview a rewind before restoring state:


``` r
gptr_checkpoints(s)
gptr_rewind(s, turn = -1, restore = "all", preview = TRUE)
gptr_rewind(s, turn = -1, restore = "all")
gptr_usage(s, by = "agent")
```

`restore = "conversation"` changes the conversation; `"workspace"` restores captured
workspace state; `"all"` requests both. Restoration covers captured objects/files and
registered checkpointers, with conflicts and unsupported changes reported. It does not undo
arbitrary external services or uncaptured side effects. Check the report and restored data.
An assignment such as `t = s` refers to the same session; use `gptr_fork()` for a branch.

For a top-level team or fan-out call in a designated history document, child code is recorded
under that statement and replay can reconstruct the children. Recording, answer caches and
usable blocks must be present; a narrative team report alone is not a replayable workflow.
See `vignette("script-as-history", package = "gptr")` for recording and summary recipes,
and `vignette("token-efficiency", package = "gptr")` for shared budgets and usage.
